# Temple Scroll Column 22 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 22 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 22:1 — "laver" vs. "basin" / "base" vs. "stand"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "laver... base" | Traditional biblical English for kiyor and kano |
| LOGOS | "laver... stand" | "Stand" clarifies the function of the base |
| PNEUMA | "basin... stand" | Modern equivalents for both terms |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "laver... base" (EMET). "Laver" is the established English term for the priestly washing vessel; "base" is traditional for kano.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 22:3 — "they shall not die" vs. "so that they do not die" vs. "or they will die"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they shall not die" | Literal rendering of the Hebrew negative |
| LOGOS | "so that they do not die" | Purpose clause conveying the intended consequence |
| PNEUMA | "or they will die" | Direct warning phrasing for impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS: "so that they do not die." Captures the purpose clause. PNEUMA's "or they will die" reverses the Hebrew syntax unnecessarily.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:5 — "court" vs. "courtyard" / "hangings" vs. "curtains"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "court... hangings" | Traditional biblical vocabulary |
| LOGOS | "courtyard... hangings" | "Courtyard" is more precise English |
| PNEUMA | "courtyard... curtains" | Modern terms throughout |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "courtyard" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) with "hangings" (EMET/LOGOS). "Courtyard" is clearer English; "hangings" is the correct term for qela'im (not curtains, which are yeriot).

**Status:** Resolved with composite.

---

## 22:10-11 — "shoulder" vs. "wing" vs. "side of the entrance"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shoulder" | Literal translation of katef |
| LOGOS | "wing" | Architectural English for a flanking section |
| PNEUMA | "side of the entrance" | Explains the spatial relationship |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's "side of the entrance." "Shoulder" is opaque; "wing" is architectural but may confuse. The clarifying phrase best communicates the layout.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA.

---

## 22:15 — "pegs" vs. "stakes" vs. "tent-pegs"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pegs" | Direct translation of yetedot |
| LOGOS | "stakes" | Alternate standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "tent-pegs and courtyard stakes" | Distinguishes the two sets by function |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "pegs" (EMET) for both occurrences. The Hebrew uses the same word (yetedot) for both tabernacle and courtyard; the translation should reflect this consistency.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
